initial.name: cancel_order
initial.description: Propose cancelling one open order by its order id from list_orders. The user approves or rejects the cancellation.

rationale.description: One to three sentences on why, shown to the user with the approval request.

initial.name: get_account
initial.description: Get the trading account: paper or live, whether trading is ready or halted, equity, cash, buying power, and profit or loss since the previous close.

initial.name: get_bars
initial.description: Get recent price bars for a US stock or a crypto pair, oldest first, with a summary: last price, high and low of the window, change, recent swing highs and lows, and the latest value of each requested indicator (sma: SMA 20, ema: EMA 20, rsi: RSI 14, macd: MACD 12/26/9, bollinger: Bollinger 20/2). Returns the last `limit` bars (default 100, at most 500) as a CSV table.

symbol.description: A US stock ticker such as AAPL, or a crypto pair such as BTC/USD (BTCUSD also works).

limit.description: How many of the most recent bars to return.

initial.name: get_positions
initial.description: List open positions with quantity, quantity available to sell, average entry price, current price, market value, and unrealized profit or loss.

initial.name: get_quote
initial.description: Get the latest bid and ask for a US stock or a crypto pair, how old the quote is, and whether its market is open.

symbol.description: A US stock ticker such as AAPL, or a crypto pair such as BTC/USD (BTCUSD also works).

initial.name: list_orders
initial.description: List the broker's open orders with their order ids, and the orders proposed through this desk today with their status and fills.

initial.name: place_order
initial.description: Propose a stock or crypto order. The user approves or rejects every order before it reaches the broker; an order that breaks a risk limit is refused with the reasons, and the limits cannot be changed from here. Give exactly one of qty or notional; notional orders are market orders. Crypto orders use time_in_force gtc or ioc and type market, limit, or stop_limit. Fractional and notional stock orders are day orders. A plain stop order is accepted only to reduce a position you hold; use stop_limit otherwise. A market order that adds exposure is sent as a limit near the quoted price, so it may not fill in a fast market. take_profit with stop_loss adds a bracket to a whole-share stock order; the bracket's exits are separate broker orders that this desk does not report, so check get_positions after a bracket may have exited. The result reports the order id and status; later fills arrive as messages.

symbol.description: A US stock ticker such as AAPL, or a crypto pair such as BTC/USD (BTCUSD also works).

qty.description: Quantity in shares or coins. Give exactly one of qty or notional.

notional.description: Dollar amount for a market order. Give exactly one of qty or notional.

limit_price.description: Required for limit and stop_limit orders.

stop_price.description: Required for stop and stop_limit orders.

time_in_force.description: Stocks: day or gtc (fractional and notional orders are day only). Crypto: gtc or ioc.

take_profit.description: Bracket take-profit limit price; whole-share stock orders only, with stop_loss.

stop_loss.description: Bracket stop-loss price; whole-share stock orders only, with take_profit.

rationale.description: One to three sentences on why, shown to the user with the approval request.

initial.name: web_fetch
initial.description: Fetch the content of a specific HTTP(S) URL and return it decoded to text.

initial.name: web_search
initial.description: Search the web for current information. Returns an optional summary answer and a list of source URLs.

queries.description: 1–4 search queries; their results are merged.
